newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA OPEN S.AFRICA TOUR ON WINNING NOTE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA OPEN S.AFRICA TOUR ON WINNING NOTE.

text.p: Australia opened their tour of South Africa on a winning note despite a brilliant 133 off 121 deliveries by local batsman Neil McKenzie on Thursday.

The touring team beat a mixture of up-and-coming and retired players by 19 runs in a relaxed one-day game with no over limitations against diamond magnate Nicky Oppenheimer's invitation XI at his private ground at Randjesfontein outside Johannesburg.
Australia were given a fine start of 124 by openers Matthew Hayden and Matthew Elliot, both easily passing the half-century mark.
Hayden hit 60 from 65 balls with five fours and two sixes, while Elliot made 91 off 106 balls with four fours and four sixes.
But the late impetus came from Steve Waugh, who retired having made 72 from just 44 deliveries with nine fours and two sixes.
Mark Taylor declared at 284 for six after 55.1 overs and Australia seemed well set for victory when the invitation XI slumped to 114 for five after seamer Paul Reiffel quickly removed both openers.
But 21-year-old McKenzie, son of former Springbok batsman Kevin McKenzie, stole the individual batting honours, lashing 19 boundaries and a six to lift the total to 265 all out.

The invitation XI's last pair survived until the day's penultimate ball when captain Jonathon Oppenheimer, Nicky's son, edged the left-arm spin of Michael Bevan to Justin Langer, who had taken over from Ian Healy behind the stumps.
Australia begin their campaign in earnest on Saturday against first-class champions Western Province at Newlands in Cape Town.
